thread:
ops-bot: PAGE: High 504 rate observed from ingress-proxy in eu-west-1. Threshold breach: 15m > 8% 5xx, paging oncall maya. Links: https://grafana.internal/ingress/eu-west-1, logs: https://logs.internal/queries/ingress-504

maya: on it. jumping in — can someone paste the most recent deploys/config changes?

jordan: saw a spike at 16:42 UTC. Initial correlate points to burst of backend timeouts from model-router pool, not raw GPU failures. sending a quick query from the edge nodes:
```
curl -s -I https://ingress.eu-west-1.redwood/api/health | head -n 1
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
```

sam: FYI I rolled a small nginx config tweak at 16:30 to increase keepalive_timeouts on the ingress hosts (PR #2345). Noticed some intermediate 502s in canary for a few minutes but assumed stable.

rachel: customer impact check — support dashboard shows ~1200 requests over last 10m failing with 504s, predominantly from a set of Chat API routes (chat.generate). Severity: degraded for some paid customers.

maya: good context. mitigation plan: 1) reduce fanout -> set ingress proxy to single-target routing for chat.generate 2) enable short-circuit fallback to model-tiles (lower-cost path) for < 8k token requests 3) roll back the keepalive tweak if needed. who's available to apply route change?

jordan: I can change the routing policy. applying a temporary routing rule now: `rbac route set chat.generate --strategy single-target --targets model-router-a`

jordan: applied. monitoring... grafana shows 504 rate dropping from 9.3% -> 3.1% in 60s. latency on the fallback path is slightly higher but errors are reduced. :thumbsup:

sam: rolling back nginx keepalive tweak across ingress nodes now (ansible job). `ansible-playbook playbooks/ingress-rollback-keepalive.yml --limit eu-west-1 -e @secrets/prod`

deploy-bot: deploy/rollback triggered by sam — playbook started (run id: play_2026_03_15_117). ETA ~2m per host, parallelism 10.

rachel: noted. customer visible errors trending down but we should be conservative with rollback. if backpressure increases, customers will notice latency.

maya: agree. jordan, keep the single-target routing for 30 minutes, then we'll assess. sam, confirm rollback finished. also start a quick traffic-sample capture for hits that still 504 so we can inspect headers and backend traces.

sam: rollback finished across all ingress hosts. logs show connections dropped to one of the model-router instances around 16:41 — suspect ephemeral connection storm. capturing pcap and http traces now (saved to /tmp/ingress-capture-1987654321.pcap).

jordan: digging into model-router logs — @model-router-1 shows repeated `upstream timeout after 30s` while other routers healthy. stack trace indicates a retry loop inside a caching layer that amplified requests to a slow origin. posting snippet:
```
[16:41:12] WARN retrying request to origin (attempt 3) cause=timeout
[16:41:12] WARN cache-miss -> origin-request (burst 120/s)
```

maya: that matches the observed blowup. mitigation: 1) add request rate limiter on ingress for routes to model-router-origin to cap amplification 2) turn off aggressive retries in the cache layer 3) follow-up: add circuit breaker thresholds to model-router upstream. Jordan, can you flip retries off?

jordan: flipped `cache.retry.max_attempts=0` in the dynamic config; change pushed to eu-west-1 runtime (cfg-id 8f3b). Confirming with a few synthetic requests.

jordan: synthetic checks show no retries and 504s continue to decline. current 5xx ~1.2% over last 5m.

rachel: communicating to support -> posting status update to status.redwood.com as "degraded: request timeouts in eu-west-1 ingress; mitigation in progress". Will add note about affected endpoints.

maya: great. now action items for post-incident: 1) hotfix PR to add circuit-breaker and rate-limiter defaults in the ingress runtime (owner: jordan, due EOD) 2) runbook update to include this amplification pattern + exact checklist for disabling retries and single-target routing (owner: maya, due tomorrow) 3) alert tuning: current 5xx alert threshold is too noisy for small bursts; propose change to 10m sustained >5% before paging (owner: rachel, propose quant by EOD) 4) customer outreach draft for affected customers (owner: sam, coordinate with support)

sam: ack on customer outreach — will sync with support and legal, should have draft in 3 hours.

jordan: opening hotfix PR now: https://git.internal/redwood/ingress-runtime/pull/2406 — includes circuit-breaker defaults and 'retry off by default' for internal origins. If CI passes I'll request an expedited review from maya.

deploy-bot: hotfix PR CI passed (build 5402).

maya: leaving a note for runbook change: add dedicated section "503/504 amplification from retries" with clear quick mitigations: single-target routing, disable retries, rollout rollback, and emergency rollback playbook link. I'll update and ping for review.

rachel: alert tuning: I'll open a metrics-alert PR to bump to 10m sustained >5% and add a secondary slack-only warning at 3% to avoid paging (PR #487 in observability).

maya: final check — current 5xx back down to <1% and no new regressions in the last 10m. keeping the incident channel open for 60m for observation, then we'll convert to follow-up thread for action items. thanks all. :heart:

jordan: quick retrospective note: add histogram of retry amplification patterns to the model-router telemetry so we can detect early pre-amplification signature.

sam: added action item: ensure pcap and traces are archived to the incident S3 bucket with metadata and link them from the runbook. (s3://incidents/1987654321/)

maya: ACTIONS SUMMARY (to be copied into postmortem):
- jordan: submit hotfix PR -> merged and staged to dedicated canary (done), schedule full rollout after validation (owner: jordan)
- maya: update runbook with new amplification section and quick mitigations (owner: maya)
- rachel: open alert tuning PR and coordinate paging thresholds (owner: rachel)
- sam: customer outreach draft + upload traces to S3 (owner: sam)
- platform: add rate-limiter + circuit-breaker templates as IaC defaults (owner: platform team, tracked in ticket INF-1299)

maya: marking incident as mitigated. converting channel to follow-up for action items. last check-in 1987654389.

ops-bot: Incident 1987654321 marked MITIGATED by maya at 1987654389. Post-incident review scheduled: 2026-03-16 15:00 UTC.
